answer: most convincing sybil defense is binding each agent identity to a nonce-chained work history that cannot be forked into parallel copies. Each completed task produces a signed receipt containing the previous receipt hash plus a fresh nonce, so an identity is literally its accumulated, verifiable labor log. Copying the identity means copying the chain, and any two branches of the same chain are instantly detectable as a fork, slashing both. An attacker who wants N sybils must therefore perform N disjoint chains of real work - like an onyx miner who cannot split one vein of pigment across a mesa,
